content: M3x12 is just fine; M3x18 and x16 are TOO LONG and will not firmly attach the cover before they bottom out.
I used a spare M3x14 screw for the cover front piece.  I had an early version that did not have a pass through hole.

I used M3x12 for mine (late Batch 1.7). Head cable cover supplied was injection moulded not 3d printed as per instruction photo. My vernier measurements indicate a max 15mm bolt thread length might work but 12mm is all I had.

Older toolheads are machined, newer ones are cast. The older ones have this hole for the cover all the way through and a M3x18 works fine here.

The newer ones do not have a through hole. I used a M3x16 here as well.
Team 8 here too, same issue, 16mm worked.
Batch 8, injection molded, M3x18 also too long. M3x16 worked snug.
Batch 5 here. M3x18 worked fine.
batch 1.8 here, injection molded head and the M3x18 was way too long. M3x16 was too long as well.  Went down to a M3x12 I had in my set and it worked great!
Same here
M3x18 was too long for mine as well, and as I didn't have a spare M3x14, I tried a M3x16 and it was perfect!
Batch 4 Injection Molded INDX. M3X18 Was Perfect Fit.
I put in a 14mm, 18 was very long. Cover was loose.
I agree with the 14mm crowd. 18 will go in and keep it from coming out, but it'll bottom out with the cable cover still being able to be wiggled

My INDX came with the injection-molded parts. I did not need to remove the cover, there was a cutout already there to install the cover screw. I also had to use an M3x14 screw since the 18mm one was clearly too long.
